## README.md
# California Park Access Tool 2020 (SCORP 2020)

Cloud-native layers derived from the **[Park Access Tool](https://www.parksforcalifornia.org/parkaccess/)**
(Parks for All Californians), produced by **GreenInfo Network** for the **California Department of Parks and
Recreation, Office of Grants and Local Services (OGALS)** to inform California's Statewide Comprehensive
Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP). This is the **2020** version (updated every five years).

Bucket: `s3://public-parks/` · Public URL base: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-parks/`

## Layers

| Layer | Path prefix | Geometry | Native H3 | What it measures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Park acres per 1,000 residents | `park-access-2020/tract-acres-per-thousand` | 8,036 census-tract polygons | 10 (9,8,0) | `PPK_tract` = park acres / 1,000 residents, classed vs. the 3-acre standard (`PPKStatus`) |
| Areas without park access | `park-access-2020/no-park-access` | 11,566 block-group polygons | 10 (9,8,0) | Areas >½ mile from a park, by population-density class (`DenStat`) |
| Areas within a half mile of a park | `park-access-2020/half-mile-access` | 1 dissolved coverage polygon | 8 (0) | ½-mile Euclidean buffer of parks — boolean "served" coverage |

Each layer publishes **GeoParquet** (`<layer>.parquet`), **PMTiles** (`<layer>.pmtiles`), and **H3 hex**
(`<layer>/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet`).

## Sources & methodology

- **Parks:** California Protected Areas Database (**CPAD 2019b**, 11/2019), adjusted by California State Parks.
- **Population:** American Community Survey **2014–2018** 5-year estimates (`B01001_001E`); block/block-group
  population from **Census 2010 (P1)** used to disaggregate block groups to blocks so large, sparsely-populated
  rural block groups are not over-distributed.
- Full methodology: <https://www.parksforcalifornia.org/methods/>

## License

**CC-BY-4.0.** The parks input (CPAD) is published under Creative Commons Attribution by GreenInfo Network; the
Census/ACS inputs are US-federal public domain. **Attribute:** GreenInfo Network and the California Department
of Parks and Recreation (OGALS), Parks for All Californians.

## Usage

### MapLibre GL JS (PMTiles)

The MapLibre `source-layer` is the **last path segment** of the dataset (e.g. `tract-acres-per-thousand`).

```js
import { Protocol } from "pmtiles";
maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile);

map.addSource("ppk", {
  type: "vector",
  url: "pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-parks/park-access-2020/tract-acres-per-thousand.pmtiles",
});
map.addLayer({
  id: "ppk-fill",
  type: "fill",
  source: "ppk",
  "source-layer": "tract-acres-per-thousand",
  paint: {
    "fill-color": [
      "match", ["get", "PPKStatus"],
      "Less than 1", "#d73027",
      "Between 1 and 3", "#fee08b",
      "Greater than 3", "#1a9850",
      "#cccccc"
    ],
    "fill-opacity": 0.7
  }
});
```

### DuckDB (GeoParquet / hex)

```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

-- Statewide population living where park provision is below the 3-acre standard
SELECT PPKStatus, SUM(TotPop) AS residents
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-parks/park-access-2020/tract-acres-per-thousand.parquet')
GROUP BY PPKStatus;

-- Hex: join to other catalog layers on h8. Per-feature totals (TotPop, Park_Acres,
-- ALAND, SqMiles, ...) are REPEATED across the cells a feature covers — dedup by
-- _cng_fid before summing:
SELECT SUM(Park_Acres) AS park_acres
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, Park_Acres
  FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-parks/park-access-2020/tract-acres-per-thousand/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
);
```

## Notes

- `PPK_tract` is undefined where population is 0 — those tracts carry `Filters = 'No Population'`.
- The `half-mile-access` hex is a **boolean coverage**: every h8 cell present is within ½ mile of a park.
- Companion nationwide dataset (TPL ParkServe) is tracked separately and hosted under `public-tpl`.
